stories.headline: Trump’s ‘let them take out Los Angeles … San Diego’ line at the Nebraska rally draws fire from California leaders
stories.summary: During Monday night’s campaign rally in Grand Island, Nebraska, President Trump, talking about the war with Iran, said, “It’s a small price to pay for keeping the world safe, keeping our country safe. They can take out a city. Let them take out Los Angeles. Let them take out San Diego.” California Democrats pounced overnight. Gov. Gavin Newsom called the president “deranged and dangerous,” Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass said a president’s job is “to protect the country, not to actively threaten it,” and San Diego Mayor Todd Gloria wrote, “We are not expendable. And we are never a ‘small price to pay.’” CBS notes that Los Angeles hosts the Space Force’s Space Systems Command and major defense contractors, and San Diego is ringed by Navy and Marine Corps bases.

stories.headline: ActBlue quietly launches a ‘passport verification program’ days after House Republicans accused it of taking foreign money
stories.summary: Democrats’ main online fundraising platform told the House on Monday that it is starting a new “passport verification program” for donors located abroad, according to a letter first reported by Fox News Digital. The move comes days after a GOP report alleged ActBlue’s passport check only confirmed that a number had the right count of characters, not that it was a valid U.S. passport, making the safeguard close to meaningless. The investigation is led by House Administration Chairman Bryan Steil with Judiciary Chairman Jim Jordan and Oversight Chairman James Comer; Jordan’s office said the change “confirms that the platform’s fraud prevention measures were not as robust” as CEO Regina Wallace-Jones told Congress. Ten ActBlue executives and founders have invoked the Fifth Amendment before GOP committees. ActBlue denies wrongdoing and calls the probe a political stunt.

stories.headline: DHS buys California’s Adelanto ICE detention complex outright for $950 million
stories.summary: The Department of Homeland Security has purchased the Adelanto immigration detention complex in Southern California’s high desert for $950 million, GEO Group announced Monday. The deal covers Adelanto East, Adelanto West and the Desert View Annex, a combined 2,644 beds. GEO will hand the properties to the federal government but keep running them under its ICE contract, which runs to December 2029 with an option to 2034. It is the latest in a string of government buyouts: DHS already paid about $1.5 billion for the California City and Otay Mesa centers and $734 million for CoreCivic sites in Minnesota and Kansas. DHS has said owning the California facilities protects ICE’s detention network from state efforts to shut down private detention. The purchases are funded by the $45 billion for detention in last year’s One Big Beautiful Bill Act.

stories.headline: Daily Wire: Washington state routed about $1.3 million in federal refugee money to CAIR’s local chapter
stories.summary: A Daily Wire review found that the Washington State chapter of the Council on American-Islamic Relations (CAIR-WA) has received about $1.29 million from the state since January 2023 under a federal Afghan-refugee legal services contract worth up to $1.35 million. The money, from the Afghanistan Supplemental Appropriations Act, made up more than 30% of the chapter’s yearly revenue and helped it grow from six staffers in 2020 toward 20 in 2026, with plans to hire a deportation defense attorney. CAIR was named an unindicted co-conspirator in the 2008 Holy Land Foundation Hamas-financing case, and Texas and Florida have declared it a terrorist organization. Health and Human Services said it asked in June for a review of CAIR affiliates’ use of federal grants. CAIR’s national office says it takes no federal money and calls the terror links “McCarthyism”; the Washington chapter did not respond.

stories.headline: Free Beacon: Michigan Senate hopeful Abdul El-Sayed has campaigned three times with a 9/11-truther imam tied to Khomeini’s regime
stories.summary: Michigan’s Democratic Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed has appeared three times this year with Mohammad Ali Elahi, imam of the Islamic House of Wisdom in Dearborn Heights, the Washington Free Beacon reports. Elahi hosted El-Sayed at his mosque in June, organized an anti-Israel “interfaith” roundtable for him in July, attended a Dearborn fundraiser that raised $350,000 last month, and gave his campaign $500. Elahi was appointed by Ayatollah Khomeini to run the Iranian Navy’s “political-ideological office” in the 1980s, helped set up a research unit for the Martyrs Foundation, which the U.S. sanctioned in 2007 for funding Hezbollah, and claimed after 9/11 that “Mossad and Israel” carried out the attacks. El-Sayed has said little publicly about the relationship, which dates to his 2018 run for governor.

stories.headline: Disney and ABC take Brendan Carr’s FCC to federal court today over its early review of all eight ABC station licenses
stories.summary: Disney and ABC go before U.S. District Judge Loren AliKhan in Washington on Tuesday morning, asking her to stop the Federal Communications Commission from fast-tracking the license reviews of all eight ABC-owned stations years ahead of schedule. Chairman Brendan Carr says the review is about stations’ duty to serve the “public interest,” not content, and notes the FCC has taken no action against the licenses yet, a point that may decide whether Disney even has standing to sue. Disney’s new CEO Josh D’Amaro authorized the fight after months of Trump posts demanding ABC lose its licenses over Jimmy Kimmel and “The View.” Republican Senate and House campaign committees filed briefs backing the FCC, citing The View’s “overwhelming” pro-Democrat tilt, while Reagan-era FCC chair Mark Fowler and libertarian groups such as Cato have sided with ABC.

stories.headline: Stabbed seven times fighting off chain snatchers, an NYPD detective rises from his wheelchair and walks out of the hospital
stories.summary: NYPD Detective Jose Mercedes left Jacobi Medical Center in the Bronx on Monday, getting up from his wheelchair and walking out on his own as hundreds of fellow officers applauded. Mercedes was off duty Friday afternoon, clearing out the trunk of his car in Norwood, when two men on an e-bike tried to rip the gold chain from his neck. He fought back and was stabbed and slashed seven times, then chased the attackers on foot for about two blocks before collapsing near East 206th Street and Rochambeau Avenue. Police Commissioner Jessica Tisch called his recovery “another incredible feat of strength and determination” and said detectives will “relentlessly pursue” the attackers, who had not been publicly identified. Tisch and Mayor Zohran Mamdani visited him in the hospital after the attack.

stories.headline: A Massachusetts felon who mailed Russian plutonium to 67 customers through his ‘Collect The Periodic Table’ business pleads guilty
stories.summary: Jacob D. Miller, 44, of South Hadley, Massachusetts, has pleaded guilty to importing nuclear material without authority, mailing hazardous materials, felon-in-possession counts for ammunition and explosives, and possession of child sexual abuse material, federal prosecutors said Monday. Through a business called Collect The Periodic Table, Miller sold element samples from his home and a third-party retailer, including radioactive plutonium from Russia that he shipped to 67 customers in the U.S. and abroad by U.S. mail, which the law forbids. Miller was already a felon: a 2002 search of his home found what looked like a rocket launcher, a pipe bomb and video of him detonating homemade explosives, and the state later warned him about selling depleted uranium on eBay. An April 2025 search turned up rifles, explosive powder and ammunition. Prosecutors cited his “long-standing and unlawful obsession” with explosives and radioactive substances.

stories.headline: Russian attacks kill 13 and wound 104 across Ukraine in a day, with Kharkiv’s toll rising to seven dead and 70 hurt
stories.summary: At least 13 people were killed and 104 injured in Russian attacks across Ukraine over the past day, regional officials said Tuesday. The Kharkiv region was hit hardest, with seven dead and 70 injured, including children, after Monday’s glide-bomb strikes on the city’s Slobidskyi district. In Kryvyi Rih, Russia hit a hospital with cheap Banderol cruise missiles, injuring four people including two medical workers. Three people were killed in Donetsk Oblast, one each in Sumy, Kherson and Dnipropetrovsk oblasts, and Russia carried out 955 attacks on 58 settlements in Zaporizhzhia Oblast. Overnight, Russia launched 137 Shahed-type drones, 49 of them jet-powered, plus decoys; Ukraine’s Air Force said 114 were shot down or jammed, with strikes recorded at 17 locations.

stories.headline: Ukraine’s biggest drone raid on Moscow in two years sets the region’s largest oil depot ablaze
stories.summary: Ukrainian drones struck the Volodarsk oil facility near the village of Konstantinovo, about 25 miles from downtown Moscow, overnight into Tuesday, according to monitoring channels and eyewitness footage showing flames and heavy smoke. Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin said at least 650 drones flew toward the capital region and that 105 were shot down as they approached the city; Russian state media called it the largest drone attack on the Moscow region in two years. The independent Russian outlet Astra says Volodarsk is the region’s biggest oil depot, handling about 3 million tons of petroleum products a year and feeding pipelines to Moscow’s major airports. The Kyiv Independent could not immediately confirm the damage. Ukraine’s Defense Ministry said Oct. 4 that more than half of Russia’s oil-refining capacity has been knocked offline.

stories.headline: Musk and Anduril’s Palmer Luckey will help lead Hegseth’s ‘Project Meridian’ study on the future of AI warfare
stories.summary: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth’s new “Project Meridian: The Future of Warfare,” a 120-day study of AI-driven and autonomous weapons, will be led by former House Speaker Newt Gingrich, SpaceX CEO Elon Musk and Anduril co-founder Palmer Luckey. Hegseth said rapid advances in AI, autonomy, directed energy and robotics “will profoundly alter the character of warfare” and that the U.S. must move decisively to dominate them. NPR reports that ethics experts, including former Bush White House ethics lawyer Richard Painter, worry the study could steer future contracts to the leaders’ own companies: SpaceX has won more than $8 billion in defense contracts this year, including its Starshield satellite network, and the Pentagon uses Grok. President Trump is scheduled to speak at an Anduril facility in Baltimore on Tuesday.

stories.headline: Apple is planning a second October launch in the last week of the month, most likely new Macs, MacRumors hears
stories.summary: On top of the Oct. 13 unveiling of a new home hub, HomePod mini and Apple TV 4K reported by Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman, Apple plans to announce more products in the final week of October, multiple sources told MacRumors. The site does not know exactly what is coming, but the likeliest candidates are Macs: the long-rumored thinner and lighter “MacBook Ultra” with an OLED display, a base 14-inch MacBook Pro with the M6 chip, and an M6 iMac. Apple has already promised a high-end Mac Studio with the M5 Ultra and 512GB of memory in “late October.” An OLED iPad mini with an A20 Pro chip, a landscape front camera and new speakers is also expected this month, timing unclear. All of that is in addition to the iPhone Duo, which goes on sale Friday, Oct. 23.

stories.headline: LEGO and Sanrio sign a multi-year deal: the first LEGO Hello Kitty and Friends sets arrive in 2027
stories.summary: The LEGO Group and Japan’s Sanrio announced Tuesday a new multi-year partnership that will put Hello Kitty and her friends into LEGO brick form for the first time. A “wide range” of LEGO Sanrio products is planned for 2027, though neither company has said what the sets will be, how many there will be, or what they will cost. LEGO’s Lena Dixen, senior vice president for global product groups, called Hello Kitty “an instantly recognizable, global lifestyle phenomenon” and said the characters pair naturally with LEGO play. The deal adds another big licensed line to LEGO’s 2027 slate, which already includes new Ninjago and Batman waves.

stories.headline: A third Canon patent for a compact RF 90mm f/2.8 IS STM macro lens surfaces, with a launch possible by early November
stories.summary: Canon Rumors has spotted another Canon patent for a compact 90mm f/2.8 macro lens, the third optical design it has seen for what it expects to be the RF 90mm f/2.8 IS STM Macro. This will not be an L-series lens, since Canon already sells the RF 100mm f/2.8L IS USM Macro; the goal is a short, light, more affordable macro. The new design uses two focusing groups with opposite optical powers that move toward and away from each other together, which helps keep image quality high and limit color fringing and blur at close distances. The site expects an announcement in the next month or so, with late October or early November most likely, though Canon has not confirmed anything.

stories.headline: Insta360 X6 firmware 1.2.35 adds 4K120 360 video and a new 360 slow-motion mode at up to 4K200
stories.summary: Insta360’s latest firmware for the X6, version 1.2.35, is its first real feature update since the camera launched in August. The regular 360 Video mode now records 4K at 120 frames per second, and a new 360 Slow-Mo mode shoots 4K at 200, 120 or 100fps, so a jump, wave or dog running past can be reframed and slowed down after the fact; 200fps played back at 25fps is eight times slower. Flat video gains 24 and 48fps, flat photos get 4:3 and 3:4 shapes, and AI Director can now be limited to a date range. The update needs the Insta360 app 2.34.5 or later, and Insta360 Studio 6.0.6 on the desktop already supports the new slow-motion files. The catch: 4K spread around a full sphere looks softer once reframed than the X6’s 8K mode.

stories.headline: Demario Davis owns his offside after penalties erased three Jets interceptions in Chicago: ‘Not reflective of our standard’
stories.summary: The Jets’ defense got its hands on nearly as many balls in Sunday’s 23–12 loss at Chicago as in its first three games combined, but penalties wiped out three interceptions, including a leaping pick by Brandon Stephens that Demario Davis negated by jumping offside. “That’s a mental penalty, a focus penalty. That can’t happen,” the veteran linebacker said. “I love the way we’re preparing, I love the way we’re fighting. Today just wasn’t reflective of our standard.” Coach Aaron Glenn brushed aside the positives, including Minkah Fitzpatrick’s slump-ending interception: “We lost a game and that’s what I’m thinking about. How do we get better?” He called anything besides the penalties “white noise.” The 1–3 Jets host the 3–1 Cleveland Browns on Sunday.

stories.headline: Tony Iommi says Ozzy was ‘carried in, basically’ to Back to the Beginning rehearsals, and he offered to play the set without him
stories.summary: In a new Guitar World interview, Black Sabbath guitarist Tony Iommi looks back on last summer’s Back to the Beginning farewell show in Birmingham, Ozzy Osbourne’s final performance before he died 17 days later at 76. Iommi first said no, not wanting another tour after The End, but agreed once he heard it was for charity. He had not seen Ozzy since the 2022 Commonwealth Games because Osbourne’s health kept him from flying. “When he came over, and we met for rehearsals, we were floored, because he was carried in, basically. I couldn’t believe how he’d deteriorated,” Iommi said. “We were all in shock.” He offered to do the whole set instrumentally so Ozzy would not have to push himself, but the Prince of Darkness refused and sang anyway.

stories.headline: Jim Bakker, the PTL televangelist whose empire collapsed in scandal and prison, dies at 86
stories.summary: Jim Bakker, who built a Christian television empire with first wife Tammy Faye and watched it collapse in scandal, died Monday at 86, his wife Lori said on the Facebook page of “The Jim Bakker Show.” No cause was given. The Bakkers went from a puppet show on a Virginia station to “The PTL Club,” launched the first Christian satellite network, and built Heritage USA, one of the world’s largest theme parks, near Fort Mill, South Carolina, on small donations from hundreds of thousands of believers. PTL fell apart in 1987 after the Charlotte Observer revealed a payment of more than $250,000 to church secretary Jessica Hahn; Bakker was convicted of fraud in 1989 and served under five years. His son Jay, a pastor with far more liberal views, wrote, “We had a very complicated relationship and he was also my father.”

stories.headline: Trumbull volleyball goes 9–0 with a four-set win at Southington; McMahon visits Tuesday
stories.summary: Trumbull High’s girls volleyball team stayed perfect with a 3–1 win at Southington on Friday (25–18, 25–20, 25–27, 25–17), its ninth straight victory to open the season, according to MaxPreps. Adriana Castillo led the Eagles with 18 kills, 12 digs and two aces, setter Lauren Yakowicz added 25 assists, six digs, four aces and two solo blocks, and Paulina Bykowski chipped in seven kills, six digs and six aces. Southington’s Lily Eidukaityte had 13 kills and 14 digs in the loss, which dropped the Blue Knights to 8–5. Trumbull has now won nine of its last 10 road matches and hosts Brien McMahon at 5:30 p.m. Tuesday. The win capped a week that also included 3–0 sweeps of Ridgefield and Stamford.

stories.headline: Babylon Bee: ‘Young, attractive blonde woman somehow manages to land job at Fox News’
stories.summary: Satire. Riffing on news that former White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt is joining Fox News, the Bee reports that “against all odds, a young, attractive blonde woman managed to land a job working at Fox News,” which commentators call “a historic first.” A fictional pundit marvels that Leavitt “had so many things working against her, being really young and hot,” and adds, “It shows how if you work hard and have a dream, even very beautiful blond women can have success.” An anonymous anchor says one of the industry’s “unwritten rules” is that “Fox News doesn’t hire gorgeous blondes,” leaving everyone “astonished she landed there, of all places.”
